problem: The ObjectNav literature is scattered across many technologies and approaches, with no consolidated overview of the state of the art, trends and gaps.
motivation: ObjectNav, with its focus on semantic navigation, is widely used for visual perception in 3D environments. A structured mapping is needed to understand the landscape and guide future research.
key_idea: Conduct a systematic literature mapping of ObjectNav, searching five databases and applying inclusion/exclusion criteria to select 28 relevant articles.
insight: Only the abstract is available, so no specific findings, trends or gaps can be reported. The abstract says only that the mapping helps identify trends, gaps and future directions.
method: Database search: five sources searched (ACM Digital Library, IEEE, Google Scholar, CAPES Journals, Web of Science)
Screening: inclusion and exclusion criteria applied, leaving 28 relevant articles
Mapping: the selected articles are categorized to describe approaches and techniques in ObjectNav
numbers_note: abstract only; survey with no experimental results
results: The systematic search and screening yielded 28 relevant ObjectNav articles. The abstract reports no further quantitative findings.
limitations: Only the abstract was available, so the detailed findings could not be verified
version: deepread-v1 (2026-09-29): full text + insight + evidence-checked numbers
